After the user selects a candidate, classify its dependencies, compare distinct interface designs and draft an RFC for the chosen direction. A proposed test deletion needs a mapping to retained or replacement behavioral coverage; no deletion may be the correct result.
improve-codebase-architecture.position: Use this skill to explore module boundaries and prepare a refactor proposal. Implementation and publication are separate actions; a GitHub issue needs the exact destination and draft confirmed first.

questions.question: Is moving code into a new file automatically a deepening?
questions.answer: No. The proposed combined interface must be smaller than the existing surfaces; otherwise the change may only reorganize code.

questions.question: Must old tests always be deleted?
questions.answer: No. Name deletions only when behavioral coverage is mapped to retained or replacement boundary tests; an evidenced none is valid.

working: Each presented candidate has evidence of coupling, a dependency category and a defensible test strategy.
The selected interface and complete RFC are reviewable before any issue is created.

insight-adversarial.summary: Stress-tests a plan, design, document, workflow, or system through distinct critic personas and synthesizes findings into a verdict.
when: You want a red-team or multi-angle challenge.
You want rigorous scrutiny of assumptions, failure points, or objections.
avoid: You want a focused review of one output; use insight-critique.
You want unseen frames rather than attacks; use insight-angles.
insight-adversarial.example: /insight-adversarial Stress-test this rollout plan against its stated dependencies and rollback constraints; identify the strongest supported objections.
steps: Classify the target and choose distinct relevant personas.
Run focused critiques with specific evidenced findings, or state no material finding supported with scope and uncertainty.
Merge convergent findings and rank up to three supported issues by actual severity, retaining disagreements.
Apply the pass rules and return the verdict and next step.

delegation.detail: Caller Options resolves inline or delegated venue for the invocation; the skill specifies no automatic fan-out.

insight-adversarial.outputs: A multi-persona critique with findings, synthesis, verdict, and next step.
overview: A plan or design seems plausible, but you want to know what different critics would attack. This skill selects distinct lenses for the target, develops specific supported objections and synthesizes them into a verdict and minimum remedies.
A lens need not find a flaw. Overlapping findings are combined with their evidence, and additional passes use new substantive perspectives on unresolved issues.
insight-adversarial.position: Use it for multi-angle stress testing. Insight-critique gives focused feedback on one output; cold-review brings fresh reviewers to actual artifacts.

questions.question: Must every persona find a different issue?
questions.answer: No. It can report no supported material finding in its inspected scope; the synthesis must not invent distinctions.

working: The verdict ranks supported objections by actual severity, preserves uncertainty and pairs material issues with concrete remedies.

insight-angles.summary: Finds less-visible frames, connections, assumptions, candidate expansions, and second-order effects around a subject.
when: You want to widen or reframe a subject.
You want connections surfaced before choosing an option.
avoid: You want implementation alternatives; use insight-explore.
You want flaw-focused review or a decision over options; use insight-adversarial or insight-cross-examine.
insight-angles.example: /insight-angles Examine this onboarding proposal. We currently optimize completion rate; surface missing stakeholder perspectives, assumptions and possible downstream effects.
steps: Frame the subject and current view.
Classify domain, type, maturity, and current trends.
Choose roster and subject-specific lenses; note skips.
Run context-appropriate passes and connect and score findings.
Return an angle map and synthesis.

delegation.detail: Selects inline or cold isolated-worker passes by subject; asks when uncertain. Quick/resolved runs are inline. Deep passes and fan-out above about six workers require Handler consent. Cold workers each handle one lens and do not delegate. Dispatch requires finite limits, monitored cancellation and a terminal/partial result; unavailable controls stop delegation. Only an existing permitted inline fallback may continue.

insight-angles.outputs: An angle map of frames, typed connections, assumptions, expansions, and second-order effects with a synthesis.
overview: A proposal feels narrow, but you do not yet know which perspective is missing. The skill selects lenses for the subject and looks for alternative frames, hidden assumptions, connections and second-order effects.

It selects lenses for the subject and returns an angle map, including candidate expansions and material assumptions. Findings remain leads to assess rather than established facts simply because they sound novel.
insight-angles.position: Choose this for missing perspectives without requiring a decision; cross-examine combines discovery with evaluation.

questions.question: Is this an implementation brainstorm?
questions.answer: Its focus is reframing and connections; use insight-explore for competing implementations.

questions.question: Does every surprising connection become a recommendation?
questions.answer: No. Connections are leads, with their relevance and implications stated; the skill does not decide or implement them.

working: The angle map distinguishes frames, connections, assumptions and possible effects.
The synthesis identifies useful implications and states the limits of coverage.

insight-assess.summary: Evaluates an approach, decision, implementation, or options against relevant criteria and recommends a course.
when: You already have an option or decision to evaluate.
You need a comparison, impact analysis, or supported recommendation.
avoid: You need to generate alternatives first; use insight-explore.
You want focused review of one output; use insight-critique.
insight-assess.example: /insight-assess Compare the supplied object-storage and database-storage proposals against migration effort, reliability, operating cost and our existing constraints.
steps: Frame the decision, objectives, constraints, and evidence.
Compare options across consistent relevant dimensions.
Use optional methods only when requested or useful.
Check alignment and identify assumptions or gaps.
Give a supported verdict, rationale, and conditions or alternatives.

delegation.detail: Defines an evidence-based assessment flow and no subagent step.

insight-assess.outputs: A verdict, rationale, conditions or alternatives, and material evidence and uncertainty.
overview: You have two storage approaches and need a reasoned choice, not more brainstorming. The assessment frames the decision and constraints, compares the options on the same relevant dimensions and traces decision-changing claims back to evidence.

Trace decision-changing claims to their observations, preserving conflicts and dependent sources. The verdict names its rationale and conditions or alternatives; if missing evidence prevents a defensible choice, RECONSIDER identifies what would resolve it.
insight-assess.position: Use insight-assess to evaluate known options. Insight-explore generates alternatives, and insight-critique reviews a specific output.

questions.question: Should every assessment use a decision tree, SWOT and impact-effort matrix?
questions.answer: No. Select an optional method only when requested or warranted, and read its reference for that route.

questions.question: Does a high benefit score override a mandatory constraint?
questions.answer: No. Evaluate feasible options under the stated obligations, keeping expected benefit separate from disruption and exposure.

working: The options are compared on consistent criteria with evidence, material uncertainty and contradictions visible.
The assessment returns a supported verdict and rationale with any conditions or alternatives.

insight-critique.summary: Reviews one existing plan, code change, architecture, or UI output and reports strengths, risks, and fixes.
when: You want focused feedback on a specific output.
You want a quality review before proceeding.
avoid: You want multi-persona stress testing; use insight-adversarial.
You need to generate or compare options; use insight-explore or insight-assess.
insight-critique.example: /insight-critique Review this API migration plan against its stated compatibility and rollback requirements.
steps: Classify the subject as code, plan, architecture, or UI.
Summarize purpose, scope, and approach.
Identify specific strengths and rank risks.
Pair risks with concrete must-fix or optional fixes.
Return the report and verdict.

delegation.detail: Caller Options resolves inline or delegated venue for the invocation.

insight-critique.outputs: A Summary, Strengths, Risks, and Fixes report with Approved, Conditional, or Not Approved verdict.
overview: You have one concrete output, such as an API migration plan, and want focused feedback before deciding what to do next. Insight-critique classifies the subject, then separates purpose and strengths from severity-ranked risks and actionable fixes.
The verdict is advisory. Approved requires only low or cosmetic risks; a critique does not itself authorize execution.
insight-critique.position: Use it for a specific plan, code change, architecture or UI. Insight-adversarial adds distinct critic lenses; option generation belongs to insight-explore.

questions.question: Can a Conditional verdict start implementation?
questions.answer: Not by itself. Execution needs the relevant approved executable plan and applicable authority.

working: The report gives a summary, specific strengths, ranked risks, concrete fixes and a verdict consistent with the risks.

insight-cross-examine.summary: Routes a subject or option set through depth-scaled deliberation, discovers angles, critiques and assesses choices, then recommends.
when: You want a recommendation across candidates or a complex decision.
You want discovery and critique combined without running every method by default.
avoid: You want only one critique, assessment, or brainstorm; use that focused skill.
You want phase-by-phase inspection of an existing plan; use plan-deep-dive.
insight-cross-examine.example: /insight-cross-examine Recommend among these three storage options for a small team. Compare migration effort, operating cost and recovery; flag missing evidence that could reverse the choice.
steps: Classify the question and evidence context; select depth.
Discover angles inline at the selected depth.
Run only selected critique, assessment, or one relevant specialist method.
For sets, compare consistently and consider justified hybrids.
Report recommendation, alternatives, uncertainty, and coverage.

delegation.detail: Normal sub-skills run inline. Large-set fan-out, L5 depth, and extra reassessment are offered for explicit consent and never automatic. Dispatch requires finite limits, monitored cancellation and a terminal/partial result; unavailable controls stop delegation. Only an existing permitted inline fallback may continue.

insight-cross-examine.outputs: A decision surface with recommendation, alternatives, decisive assumptions, coverage, and analysis trail.
overview: You need a recommendation among candidates and the available evidence is uneven. This workflow adjusts its depth to the question, discovers useful angles, then compares the choices and any justified combinations against consistent criteria.

It reuses applicable findings, evaluates selected options consistently and may recommend deferral when the evidence is insufficient. Deeper reassessment or large fan-out is offered rather than launched automatically.
insight-cross-examine.position: Use a focused insight skill for a single method; choose cross-examine for a recommendation that combines methods.

questions.question: What if the problem is missing evidence rather than missing options?
questions.answer: Name the decision-changing evidence gap instead of generating extra candidates to fill it.

questions.question: What if the evidence cannot support a winner?
questions.answer: Recommend a specific evidence-gathering step or deferral. More candidate options do not resolve an evidence gap.

working: The decision surface includes a recommendation, alternatives, the weak assumption and what could change the result.
Coverage, intentionally skipped angles and material uncertainty are stated.

insight-explore.summary: Generates distinct approaches to a problem and compares them before a plan is chosen.
when: You want a brainstorm of ways to solve a problem.
You need plausible alternatives before committing.
avoid: You have fixed options to evaluate; use insight-assess.
You need a detailed implementation plan; use plan-create.
insight-explore.example: /insight-explore Explore ways to add offline support to this app, keeping existing authentication and a two-week delivery constraint in view.
steps: Clarify constraints, requirements, and preferences.
Generate distinct approaches, including standard, performance-oriented, and minimal options where useful.

Collect every actual feasible candidate from the lenses and justified additions; compare the complete set on developer experience, robustness, timeline and alignment. Keep bounded-search evidence for single-option, no-feasible-option or unresolved outcomes without inventing alternatives.
Recommend a supported option or report a constrained or unresolved outcome, then suggest the next useful step.

delegation.detail: Specifies ideation and comparison, with no subagent step.

insight-explore.outputs: Distinct options, comparison, recommendation, and proposed next step; no code or implementation plan.
overview: You know the problem but have not chosen how to solve it. The skill separates requirements from preferences and searches through different lenses, such as a familiar pattern, a performance-oriented approach and a minimal approach, before comparing the feasible candidates.

Compare the entire candidate set on developer experience, robustness, timeline and alignment. Recommend a winner only if evidence supports one; otherwise explain the constrained or unresolved outcome, search scope and decisive gap.
insight-explore.position: Use insight-explore before committing to a direction. Insight-assess evaluates established options in greater depth, and plan-create designs the chosen implementation.

questions.question: What if the bounded search finds fewer than three feasible options?
questions.answer: Report the actual one- or zero-option result and its evidence and gaps. Do not invent options or a winner to meet a count.

working: The result distinguishes constraints and compares all actual candidates rather than only the first three.
A recommendation is supported by the comparison, or the unresolved outcome and decisive gap are explicit.

insight-premortem.summary: Imagines a plan has failed and identifies plausible causes, evidence gaps, and ways to prevent or detect them.
when: You want to identify future failure paths before committing.
You need warning signs and response triggers for a proposed plan.
avoid: The failure has happened and needs causal investigation; use insight-root-cause.
You want broad post-implementation learning; use insight-retro.
insight-premortem.example: /insight-premortem Assume this migration missed its six-month deadline; use the attached plan and dependencies to identify plausible paths and warning signs.
steps: Name the plan, constraints, intended result, and observable failure.
Generate plausible causes before mitigations.
Check causes against assumptions, evidence, counterevidence, and missing perspectives.
Prioritize and propose prevention, warnings, responses, and residual risks.

delegation.detail: Inline by default. Workers only when requested or host-permitted and a specific evidence gap justifies them; tasks are bounded, read-only, non-overlapping, and have no nested delegation.

insight-premortem.outputs: Failure paths, evidence status, proposed mitigations and warning signs, residual risks, and gaps; no plan edits.
overview: Before committing to a plan, imagine that its intended outcome has failed at a specified future point. Premortem asks what plausible paths could have produced that failure before jumping to mitigations.

The imagined outcome is a framing device, not proof of likelihood. Each material path is checked against assumptions, evidence and counterevidence, then paired with a warning sign and response trigger where possible.
insight-premortem.position: Use it before a future decision. Insight-root-cause examines an event that occurred; insight-retro draws broader lessons after implementation.

questions.question: Does this edit the plan or assign work?
questions.answer: No. It returns proposed changes, residual risks and unresolved ownership for the caller to decide.

working: The output distinguishes hypotheses from observations and identifies material paths, proposed responses, residual risks and evidence gaps.

insight-reference-class.summary: Forecasts an outcome from comparable completed cases and explains differences from the current plan's estimate.
when: You want an outside-view forecast based on past cases.
You want to check whether a schedule, cost, or outcome estimate is optimistic.
avoid: You want to assess whether more research is worth its cost; use insight-value-of-information.
You lack a defensible comparison set and need a numeric forecast.
insight-reference-class.example: /insight-reference-class Estimate the likely duration of this migration using traceable completed migrations of similar size. Compare the observed range with our six-week plan.
steps: Define outcome, units, horizon, decision, and comparability criteria.
Build a traceable set of comparable completed cases, noting failures and exclusions.
Show the supported observed range or distribution.
Compare with the inside view and explain adjustments, limits, and what could change the estimate.

delegation.detail: Inline by default. Workers only when requested or host-permitted and a specific evidence gap justifies them; useful slices include case retrieval, selection challenge, and calculation checks.

insight-reference-class.outputs: An outside-view estimate or evidence-insufficient conclusion with sources, limits, adjustments, and sensitivity.
overview: A schedule or cost estimate looks plausible from inside the project, but you want to compare it with what happened elsewhere. Define comparable completed cases first, then show their observed outcomes and the limits of applying them here.

Show the observed range or supported distribution, including failures and selection limitations. Adjustments for the present case need evidence and do not turn historical coverage into a guaranteed probability.
insight-reference-class.position: Use this for an outside-view estimate; use insight-value-of-information to decide whether more research is worth its cost.

questions.question: What if there is no defensible comparison set?
questions.answer: Report insufficient evidence and a path to collect it rather than manufacture a numeric forecast.

questions.question: Can a small sample justify a precise percentile?
questions.answer: Only if the data support it. Label small or biased samples and do not invent cases or percentiles to make the result look complete.

working: The report traces cases and exclusions to sources and explains their comparability.
The estimate or evidence-insufficient conclusion states sensitivity, adjustments and limitations.

insight-retro.summary: Reviews significant completed implementation work to map impact, capture patterns, check documentation, and list follow-up work.
when: A substantial implementation has finished and its effects should be recorded.
You need to check documentation, reusable knowledge, difficulty, and technical debt.
avoid: You only want candidate skill gaps; use insight-skill-gap.
There is no reliable inventory of completed changes yet.
insight-retro.example: /insight-retro Review the completed authentication rollout using the approved plan, current diff and verification results; identify documentation drift and follow-up debt.
steps: Map changed packages, files, interfaces, and effects.
Resolve actual repository documentation conventions and catalog scope; missing sidecar conventions or indexes do not establish defects or an empty library.
Extract reusable patterns and recommend skill, documentation, or no action.
Audit documentation and knowledge items against the change map.
Assess execution difficulty and technical debt.
Return findings with gate status and unverified criteria.

delegation.detail: Specifies a retrospective workflow and no subagent step.

insight-retro.outputs: Blast-radius summary, pattern and documentation findings, knowledge updates, difficulty notes, technical debt, and gate status.
overview: A substantial implementation is finished, but its effects and loose ends are spread across files, checks and conversation. The retrospective starts with an inventory of what actually changed, then uses it to inspect documentation, reusable patterns, difficulties and technical debt.

The retrospective reports observations and concrete follow-ups; fixes are separate work. Gate outcomes and unverified acceptance criteria remain visible, and a misleading documentation finding cites both the claim and contradictory code.
insight-retro.position: Use insight-retro for a broad post-implementation account; insight-skill-gap focuses specifically on candidate skill improvements.

questions.question: Is a missing YON sidecar automatically a documentation defect?
questions.answer: No. First establish the repository's documentation conventions; apply sidecar thresholds only when that convention is adopted or requested.

questions.question: What if the skill catalog cannot be found?
questions.answer: Keep skill proposals provisional and state that duplicate coverage is incomplete; a missing index is not evidence of an empty library.

working: The report ties documentation, patterns and debt to the actual changed scope and names actionable follow-ups.
Skipped gates, unverified criteria and missing catalog coverage are disclosed rather than implied clean.

insight-root-cause.summary: Investigates an observed or recurring problem by tracing evidence-linked causes and competing explanations.
when: You want to explain why an observed problem occurred.
You need supported causes separated from contributors and open hypotheses.
avoid: The event is hypothetical; use insight-premortem.
You want broad lessons after an implementation; use insight-retro.
insight-root-cause.example: /insight-root-cause Use these import logs, expected behavior and failure times to investigate why the scheduled job stops early.
steps: Describe the event, expected behavior, timeframe, scope, and impact.
Build causal hypotheses with evidence and a disconfirming check for each link.
Challenge timing, mechanism, and competing explanations.
Report supported causes separately and propose a test or countermeasure without running it.

delegation.detail: Inline by default. Workers only when requested or host-permitted and a specific evidence gap justifies them; possible slices include timeline, alternative causes, and disconfirmation.

insight-root-cause.outputs: Evidence-linked causal account, unresolved hypotheses, and proposed checks or countermeasures.
overview: A recurring import stops early and the team has several explanations. Root-cause analysis establishes what was observed, when and under what conditions, then connects each causal hypothesis to supporting evidence and a disconfirming check.
Alternative or interacting causes can branch. If evidence cannot distinguish them, return an unresolved causal question and a proposed discriminating check instead of forcing a single answer.
insight-root-cause.position: Use it for an observed problem. Premortem considers hypothetical future failure; retro looks more broadly at completed work.

questions.question: Must I ask exactly five whys?
questions.answer: No. Continue to supported actionable conditions or the evidence boundary; neither a fixed count nor a single cause is required.

working: The account separates supported causes, contributors and unresolved hypotheses, and proposes a test or countermeasure without executing it.

insight-skill-gap.summary: Compares recent work with the existing skill index to find reusable patterns that are missing or under-covered.
when: You want to know whether recent work exposed a skill gap.
A retrospective identified patterns worth comparing with existing skills.
avoid: You want to create or edit a skill now; use skill-smith after choosing a proposal.
You need a full retrospective of changes and technical debt; use insight-retro.
insight-skill-gap.example: /insight-skill-gap Review the recent cache migration and determine whether its recurring invalidation decisions are already covered by the installed skill catalog.
steps: Gather recent work and summarize patterns and technologies.

Resolve the actual supplied or host/repository catalog and record its scope before duplicate checks. If unavailable, keep candidates provisional and duplicate coverage incomplete; missing is not empty.
Classify patterns as covered, incomplete, or absent and apply reuse criteria.
Present a targeted update or new-skill proposal for approval.
Only after approval, apply selected creation or updates through Skill Smith and the canonical write owner.

delegation.detail: Specifies a scan and proposal flow and no subagent step.

insight-skill-gap.outputs: Coverage findings and justified proposals, followed by skill creation or targeted updates only when approved.
overview: Recent work exposed a repeated decision or pitfall and you wonder whether it belongs in a reusable skill. Compare that pattern with the actual skill catalog before proposing an update or a new entry.
A missing catalog is incomplete duplicate coverage, not proof that the library is empty. Proposals identify the reuse case and the specific missing sections.
insight-skill-gap.position: Use this to find reusable skill gaps after work; use insight-retro for the broader implementation retrospective.

questions.question: Does the scan create skills automatically?
questions.answer: No. It presents proposals for approval; selected work then follows the skill authoring owner.

questions.question: What if the catalog cannot be found?
questions.answer: Keep candidates provisional and say duplicate coverage is incomplete. A missing index does not mean no relevant skill exists.

working: Candidates are classified as covered, incomplete or absent against the actual index.
A proposal explains reuse and scope, or identifies incomplete duplicate checking.

insight-test-assumption.summary: Designs a bounded test that could support or disprove a decision-critical assumption; it does not run the test.
when: A decision depends on an uncertain assumption.
You need a test with observable outcomes and a decision rule.
avoid: You want to decide whether information is worth its cost; use insight-value-of-information.
You want the test executed, participants recruited, or spending/deployment performed.
insight-test-assumption.example: /insight-test-assumption Design a bounded test of whether new customers can complete the supplied onboarding flow without help; the decision is whether to remove assisted setup.
steps: Name the decision, assumption, current evidence, and consequence if false.
Use existing evidence or design the smallest credible bounded test.
Set support, disconfirmation, and inconclusive criteria before results.
Return the test card, bounds, costs, risks, and interpretation limits.

delegation.detail: Inline by default. Workers only when requested or host-permitted and a specific evidence gap justifies them; possible slices include evidence retrieval, test design, and challenging the measurement or rule.

insight-test-assumption.outputs: A proposed test card and decision rule; no experiment execution, recruitment, spending, or deployment.
overview: A product decision depends on a belief that new customers can complete onboarding without help. The skill identifies what decision would change, uses existing evidence if sufficient and otherwise designs a bounded check that could support, contradict or leave the belief unresolved.

Before results, specify what would support, contradict or leave the assumption unresolved and what each outcome would mean for the decision. A proxy is indirect evidence, and a pilot does not establish general validity.
insight-test-assumption.position: Use this to design a discriminating check. Insight-value-of-information addresses whether additional information is worth its cost; running a test requires separate authority.

questions.question: What if results already exist without a prior decision rule?
questions.answer: Label the interpretation exploratory or post-hoc. Do not claim a pre-agreed test passed; propose a prospective check only if further evidence could affect the decision.

working: The test card connects a falsifiable assumption to observable outcomes and the decision each would change.
It states time, cost, risks, measurement limits and unknowns without inventing precision or executing the test.

insight-value-of-information.summary: Assesses whether information could improve a pending choice enough to justify research, testing, and delay costs.
when: You are unsure whether to research or test before deciding.
You need to compare a decision-changing signal's value with its acquisition cost.
avoid: You need a test designed; use insight-test-assumption.
You want information purchased or research performed; this skill evaluates but does not acquire it.
insight-value-of-information.example: /insight-value-of-information Compare deciding the launch date now with this proposed customer pilot, using the attached deadline, costs and possible decisions.
steps: Frame feasible actions, current best choice, horizon, and uncertain inputs.
Describe information, signals, reliability, action changes, and costs.
Calculate EVSI/EVPI only when probabilities, payoffs, and signal accuracy are supported.
Recommend gathering information, deciding now, or remaining unresolved, with a stopping rule.

delegation.detail: Inline by default. Workers only when requested or host-permitted and a specific evidence gap justifies them; useful slices include decision model, source reliability, and arithmetic checks.

insight-value-of-information.outputs: A supported information-value estimate or qualitative switching conditions with cost, gaps, and stopping rule.
overview: You must choose a launch date and wonder whether a pilot is worth delaying the decision. This skill asks what signal the pilot could produce, which action would change for each signal, and whether the benefit could exceed acquisition and delay costs.

With defensible probabilities, payoffs and signal accuracy it can calculate expected information value and check the perfect-information upper bound. Otherwise it gives qualitative switching conditions and missing evidence instead of invented numbers.
insight-value-of-information.position: Use it to decide whether more information is worth pursuing. Insight-test-assumption can design a selected test; this assessment does not launch it.

questions.question: What if the result arrives after the decision deadline?
questions.answer: It cannot improve that choice if it cannot affect the action in time, although a separate learning or compliance purpose may remain.

working: The recommendation says gather, decide now or unresolved, and identifies switching conditions, costs, gaps and a stopping rule.

investigate.summary: Gathers facts without changing the target.
when: You need to understand dependencies or behavior.
You want an evidence-backed code map.
avoid: You are asking for implementation or a plan.
investigate.example: /investigate Trace how an uploaded file reaches storage, including validation, callers and configuration. Report the relevant paths and unresolved links.
steps: Identify target and read entry points.
Trace relevant usages, imports and patterns.
Report findings, source anchors and gaps without making changes.

delegation.detail: Caller Options can select inline or delegated investigation.

overview: Before choosing a change, you need to know where the behavior lives and what depends on it. This read-only pass starts at relevant entry points and follows call sites and imports into a source-backed map.
The report identifies concrete files, patterns and constraints, and makes evidence gaps visible. It does not turn fact gathering into a plan or implementation.
investigate.position: Use debug-task for executed reproduction of a specific failure and investigate for a source-backed map.

questions.question: Can investigation choose the future architecture?
questions.answer: It supplies facts for that decision; evaluation and planning are separate tasks.

questions.question: Does this run or fix the suspected failure?
questions.answer: No. It gathers facts without changes. Use a bounded debugging workflow if executed reproduction is needed.

working: Findings name relevant paths and their relationships.
The report distinguishes observed behavior from unresolved paths or unknowns.

json-canvas.summary: Create or edit JSON Canvas diagrams with nodes and edges.
when: Build a mind map
Connect notes in a canvas
avoid: Editing Markdown notes or Bases
json-canvas.example: /json-canvas Create a mind map in a new .canvas file for the supplied project topics, with dependencies connected by labelled edges.
steps: Identify the diagram's content and relationships
Create valid nodes and edges with suitable positions
Check IDs, references and JSON structure
Validate the candidate before saving; preserve unrelated content and recovery, recheck current identity and read back the protected write. New files use exclusive creation.
Open the canvas when available to inspect the layout

delegation.detail: The skill defines no subagent step; host rules still apply.

overview: You want to arrange project topics spatially and show how they connect. A Canvas file stores positioned nodes and edges; the skill prepares the diagram, checks unique identifiers and edge references, and then saves the validated candidate through the protected write boundary.

For edits, preserve unknown and unrelated content, validate the complete candidate and protect a recoverable preimage. Recheck the target revision before replacement and read back the result; a new file is created exclusively.
json-canvas.position: Use json-canvas for a spatial diagram, obsidian-bases for views over note properties, and obsidian-markdown for the notes themselves.

questions.question: Is valid JSON enough to establish a usable canvas?
questions.answer: No. IDs must be unique, edges must reference existing nodes, and required fields and supported values must also be checked; a visual inspection can assess layout.

working: The saved canvas parses and its nodes and edges satisfy the structural checks.
Unrelated existing content is preserved and the persisted result is read back.

map-check.summary: Run a read-only conformance check on a bounded knowledge map.
when: Check a map's health
Inspect graph conformance
avoid: Applying repairs or claiming an unqualified all-clear
map-check.example: /map-check Check the declared project scope at this path and report the checked inventory, findings and omissions.
steps: Identify the scope and load the governing rules
Run the bundled checker with the appropriate inventory
Inspect findings and operational errors separately
Report exactly what was and was not checked
If map-rules is absent, keep the compiled checker boundary and report manual rule/provenance review unavailable.
In DEGRADED mode, supply the established scope root with a contained relative root-map locator; nested-target walk-up is not promised.

Require every governed Markdown entrypoint to be readable, even for a plain link without a fragment. Keep invalid declarations and unreadable or capped resolution distinct from qualified-clean; manual rulings never rewrite the deterministic verdict.

delegation.detail: The skill defines no subagent step; host rules still apply.

overview: You have a declared Map Your Knowledge scope and want to know whether its ownership and navigation conform to the implemented checks. Map-check runs a bounded, read-only checker and reports inventory, mode, findings and omissions.
